text: Geopolitical tension spikes can lift population cortisol, worsening sleep and anxiety; such collective stress may lower confidence and health, so public‑health monitoring of community stress can aid early interventions.

Geopolitical spikes simultaneously drive safe‑haven inflows and raise population cortisol, creating a feedback loop where market narratives amplify health stress; tracking financial sentiment could serve as an early indicator for public‑health interventions.

Geopolitical flashpoints pump cortisol like a meme virus—sleep‑deprived brains scramble for safe‑haven assets, then meme‑stock mania follows. Tracking population‑level sleep could become the next early‑warning gauge for capital flows.
